title: Objects Inside Objects
summary: Learn how Java classes nest references to other custom objects as member fields, navigating pointer chains and preventing NullPointerExceptions.
learningObjectives: Store references to custom user-defined classes as member fields of another class
Trace multi-hop reference dot-navigation (e.g., student.getAddress().getCity()) in heap memory
Defend against NullPointerException when accessing nested object properties
Implement deep vs shallow constructors and defensive copy patterns
expectedOutcomes: You can construct multi-tiered object graphs combining primitive and reference member fields
You can confidently trace nested heap allocations and avoid null-reference pitfalls

activities.title: Everyday Analogy: Russian Matryoshka Nesting Dolls & Wallets

realWorldMetaphor.scenario: Think about your wallet. The wallet itself is a leather object. Inside the wallet is a credit card object. Inside the credit card object is an embedded security chip object. Inside the security chip is encrypted account data.
realWorldMetaphor.mapping: In Java, an outer object (`Person`) does not literally store the entire inner object's bytes inside its own memory slot. It holds a 64-bit reference address (pointer) pointing to the `Wallet` object on the heap, which in turn points to the `CreditCard` object, which points to the `Chip` object.
realWorldMetaphor.takeaway: Objects inside objects are connected via reference links. Each link in the chain can be independently inspected, swapped, or null-checked.

activities.title: Memory Layout of Nested Object References
Multi-Level Object Composition: Student, Address, and Contact
activities.explanation: Student cleanly composes Address and ContactInfo. Each class has a single responsibility and is independently testable.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `Address` and `ContactInfo` are defined as standalone domain entities.
`Student` declares fields referencing instances of both classes.
In `printDossier()`, `Student` delegates formatting directly to the nested objects.
`main` instantiates components and wires them together cleanly.

activities.title: Null-Safe Navigation and Cascading Inspection
activities.explanation: Guarding against null nested objects avoids sudden runtime crashes when properties are optional or not yet populated.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `Box` allows `dimensions` to be passed as null for unmeasured boxes.
Both measured and unmeasured boxes execute safely without NullPointerException.

questions.question: When an object of class A has an instance field of class B, what does A physically hold?
options: A complete byte-for-byte copy of B inside A's memory block
A reference pointer to B's memory location in the heap
A copy of B's class file
questions.explanation: In Java, object fields hold reference pointers (addresses) pointing to objects allocated on the heap.

questions.question: What happens if you evaluate 'person.getAccount().getBalance()' when person.getAccount() returns null?
options: A NullPointerException is thrown at runtime
questions.explanation: Calling any method on a null reference throws a java.lang.NullPointerException at runtime.

questions.question: How can two different Person objects share the exact same Address object?
options: By both having their address fields point to the same heap memory address
Java does not permit sharing objects
questions.explanation: Multiple reference variables can point to the exact same object in heap memory.

questions.question: What is the recommended visibility modifier for nested object reference fields in a well-encapsulated class?
questions.explanation: Instance fields should be private to protect internal state and enforce encapsulation.

questions.question: What is a 'deep copy' when cloning an object containing nested objects?
options: Copying only the memory reference addresses
Recursively creating brand-new duplicate instances of all nested objects
Converting the object to a String
questions.explanation: A deep copy creates new instances of nested objects so modifications to the copy do not alter the original.

questions.question: Given: `car.getEngine().getTurbo().boost()`. What software design principle discourages very long chains of getters?
options: Law of Demeter (Principle of Least Knowledge)
questions.explanation: The Law of Demeter states that a module should not know about the innards of the objects it manipulates.

questions.question: If you don't initialize a custom object field in a class, what is its default value?
questions.explanation: All uninitialized object reference fields in Java default to `null`.

questions.question: How should a class validate that a mandatory nested dependency was passed to its constructor?
questions.explanation: Objects.requireNonNull(...) is the idiomatic, standard Java way to fail fast if a mandatory collaborator is null.

questions.question: Can an object hold a reference to an object of the same class (e.g. `Node next`)?
options: Yes, this is the foundational pattern for linked lists and tree structures
Only if the class is abstract
questions.explanation: Self-referencing structures like `class Node { Node next; }` are fundamental to data structures like linked lists.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of decomposing a large God-Class into smaller nested classes?
options: Single Responsibility Principle, high cohesion, and reusable components
questions.explanation: Decomposition promotes the Single Responsibility Principle and creates clean, reusable, focused components.

questions.question: What is the Law of Demeter (Principle of Least Knowledge) and how does it relate to nested objects?
questions.answer: The Law of Demeter states that a method should only call methods on: (1) its own fields, (2) objects passed as parameters, (3) objects created locally, or (4) global singletons. It warns against long getter chains like `order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode()`. Instead, `order` should delegate: `order.getDeliveryZipCode()`.
questions.expectedAnswer: The Law of Demeter states that a method should only call methods on: (1) its own fields, (2) objects passed as parameters, (3) objects created locally, or (4) global singletons. It warns against long getter chains like `order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode()`. Instead, `order` should delegate: `order.getDeliveryZipCode()`.
questions.keyTakeaway: Talk only to your immediate friends; don't talk to strangers through long getter chains.
keyPoints: Talk only to your immediate friends; don't talk to strangers through long getter chains.

questions.question: What is the difference between a shallow copy and a deep copy of an object graph?
questions.answer: A shallow copy creates a new outer object, but copies reference pointers to existing nested objects (sharing them). A deep copy recursively instantiates brand-new copies of all nested objects, guaranteeing complete independence from the original.
questions.expectedAnswer: A shallow copy creates a new outer object, but copies reference pointers to existing nested objects (sharing them). A deep copy recursively instantiates brand-new copies of all nested objects, guaranteeing complete independence from the original.
questions.keyTakeaway: Shallow copy shares nested references; deep copy clones the entire object graph.
keyPoints: Shallow copy shares nested references; deep copy clones the entire object graph.

questions.question: How do you protect immutable outer classes that contain mutable nested objects?
questions.answer: You must employ defensive copying: (1) In the constructor, clone or copy the mutable parameter before assigning it to the field, and (2) In getter methods, return a fresh copy or an unmodifiable view rather than the original internal reference.
questions.expectedAnswer: You must employ defensive copying: (1) In the constructor, clone or copy the mutable parameter before assigning it to the field, and (2) In getter methods, return a fresh copy or an unmodifiable view rather than the original internal reference.
questions.keyTakeaway: Defensive copying in constructor and getters prevents callers from mutating private inner state.
keyPoints: Defensive copying in constructor and getters prevents callers from mutating private inner state.

questions.question: Why is composing small classes better than one giant class with 30 primitive fields?
questions.answer: Grouping related fields into value objects (e.g. `Address`, `Money`, `GeoPoint`) improves cohesion, ensures validation logic lives in one place, eliminates code duplication, and makes methods much easier to read and maintain.
questions.expectedAnswer: Grouping related fields into value objects (e.g. `Address`, `Money`, `GeoPoint`) improves cohesion, ensures validation logic lives in one place, eliminates code duplication, and makes methods much easier to read and maintain.
questions.keyTakeaway: Domain-driven value objects turn primitive obsession into expressive, validated components.
keyPoints: Domain-driven value objects turn primitive obsession into expressive, validated components.

questions.question: How does garbage collection handle nested objects when the outer object is discarded?
questions.answer: When the outer object becomes unreachable, the reference pointers to nested objects are also released. If no other living roots point to those nested objects, they too become eligible for garbage collection automatically.
questions.expectedAnswer: When the outer object becomes unreachable, the reference pointers to nested objects are also released. If no other living roots point to those nested objects, they too become eligible for garbage collection automatically.
questions.keyTakeaway: GC traverses the reachability graph; unreferenced nested objects are reclaimed.
keyPoints: GC traverses the reachability graph; unreferenced nested objects are reclaimed.

questions.question: What are the performance implications of deep object nesting in the JVM?
questions.answer: Deep nesting introduces memory overhead due to 16-byte object headers for each sub-object and reference pointer indirection, which can reduce CPU cache locality compared to contiguous flat data structures.
questions.expectedAnswer: Deep nesting introduces memory overhead due to 16-byte object headers for each sub-object and reference pointer indirection, which can reduce CPU cache locality compared to contiguous flat data structures.
questions.keyTakeaway: Every object has header overhead and pointer indirection, though the clean architecture usually outweighs minor overhead.
keyPoints: Every object has header overhead and pointer indirection, though the clean architecture usually outweighs minor overhead.

practiceProblems.title: Employee Profile with Nested Address
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Complete the `Address` and `Employee` classes below. `Address` contains `street` and `zipCode`. `Employee` contains `name`, `empId`, and an `Address`. Implement `getProfileSummary()` on `Employee` to return `'[EMP-101] John Doe, Residing at: 123 Main St, 94105'`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput: [EMP-101] John Doe, Residing at: 123 Main St, 94105

practiceProblems.title: Three-Tier Vehicle Telemetry System
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a 3-tier nested telemetry system from scratch:
1. Class `GpsCoordinate`: holds `private double lat, lon`. Constructor accepts `double lat, double lon`. Method `public String toFormattedString()` returns `'Lat: ' + lat + ', Lon: ' + lon`.
2. Class `TelemetryUnit`: holds `private int speedKmh` and `private GpsCoordinate coordinate`. Constructor accepts `int speedKmh, GpsCoordinate coordinate`. Method `public void logTelemetry()` prints `'[Telemetry] Speed: ' + speedKmh + ' km/h | Position: (' + coordinate.toFormattedString() + ')'`.
3. Class `FleetTruck`: holds `private String truckId` and `private TelemetryUnit telemetry`. Constructor accepts `String truckId, TelemetryUnit telemetry`. Method `public void pingServer()` prints `'[Truck ' + truckId + '] Broadcasting packet...'` and calls `telemetry.logTelemetry()`.
4. In `Main`, create GPS coordinate (40.7128, -74.0060), telemetry unit with 85 km/h, and truck 'TRK-900'. Call `pingServer()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
[Truck TRK-900] Broadcasting packet...
[Telemetry] Speed: 85 km/h | Position: (Lat: 40.7128, Lon: -74.006)
hints: Construct GpsCoordinate first, pass it into TelemetryUnit, then pass TelemetryUnit into FleetTruck.
FleetTruck delegates logging to TelemetryUnit, which delegates position formatting to GpsCoordinate.

practiceProblems.title: Null-Safe Bank Profile Inspector
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a null-safe banking inspector from scratch:
1. Class `CreditScore`: holds `private int score`. Constructor accepts int. Method `public int getScore()` returns score.
2. Class `CustomerProfile`: holds `private String fullName` and `private CreditScore creditScore` (which may be null!). Constructor accepts `String fullName, CreditScore creditScore`.
   - Method `public void printRiskAssessment()`:
     - If `creditScore != null` and `creditScore.getScore() >= 700`, print `'Customer [' + fullName + ']: Low Risk (Score: ' + creditScore.getScore() + ')'`.
     - If `creditScore != null` and `creditScore.getScore() < 700`, print `'Customer [' + fullName + ']: High Risk (Score: ' + creditScore.getScore() + ')'`.
     - If `creditScore == null`, print `'Customer [' + fullName + ']: Risk Unknown (No Credit File)'`.
3. In `Main`, test with: (1) Alice with score 740, (2) Bob with score 620, (3) Charlie with null credit score. Call `printRiskAssessment()` on each.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Customer [Alice]: Low Risk (Score: 740)
Customer [Bob]: High Risk (Score: 620)
Customer [Charlie]: Risk Unknown (No Credit File)
hints: Always check if creditScore is null before invoking creditScore.getScore().

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Cascading NullPointerException in Order Receipt
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The code below crashes with a `NullPointerException` because the order was created with a null `ShippingAddress`, yet `printInvoice()` unconditionally dereferences it without checking. Fix `printInvoice()` to check if `address` is null. If null, print `'Ship To: Digital Delivery / Pickup'`. Otherwise print `'Ship To: ' + address.getFormatted()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Order: ORD-DIGITAL-99 | Total: $29.99
Ship To: Digital Delivery / Pickup
hints: Wrap the address print statement with `if (address != null)`.
Provide the fallback `Digital Delivery / Pickup` when address is null.

practiceProblems.title: Audio Workstation Hardware Rack Builder
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Design a digital audio workstation (DAW) audio hardware chain from scratch:
1. Class `AudioPreamp`: holds `private String brand` and `private double gainDb`. Constructor initializes both. Method `public String getPreampSpecs()` returns brand + ' (' + gainDb + 'dB gain)'.
2. Class `AudioInterface`: holds `private String model`, `private int sampleRateKhz`, and `private AudioPreamp preamp`. Constructor initializes all three. Method `public void describeInterface()` prints `'[Interface] ' + model + ' @ ' + sampleRateKhz + 'kHz with Preamp: ' + preamp.getPreampSpecs()`.
3. Class `StudioDesk`: holds `private String studioName` and `private AudioInterface audioInterface`. Constructor initializes both.
   - Method `public void powerUpStudio()` prints `'=== Studio: ' + studioName + ' Online ==='` and calls `audioInterface.describeInterface()`.
4. In `Main`, create a preamp ('Focusrite Scarlett Pre', 56.0), an audio interface ('Clarett+ 2Pre', 192, preamp), and studio ('Abbey Sound', audioInterface). Call `powerUpStudio()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
=== Studio: Abbey Sound Online ===
[Interface] Clarett+ 2Pre @ 192kHz with Preamp: Focusrite Scarlett Pre (56.0dB gain)
hints: Follow the 3-tier object graph: StudioDesk -> AudioInterface -> AudioPreamp.
Verify exact output punctuation and formatting.
